test_round.name: round 1
test_round.note: 24 October, the data report's factorial tests; widened 26 October to every channel and 11 factors (one pooled, channel-aware model: every Short on every channel, exploration Shorts aside, takes an arm of each factor, 50/50 and independent, writer.test_plan; a channel leaves out franchise, and the hour on the Americas grid). analytics/round.csv judges each factor adjusted for the channel, exploration and every other factor (drivers.round_verdicts): winner (90% interval clear, 10 a side, the halves agree), even (interval within 0.87x to 1.15x, 20 a side) or no clear difference at per_arm a side; a winner is kept and challenged 1 Short in 5, an even factor leaves the round. "lab" is the look dimension's newest lab option on the day (looks.arm_option). fx_* (looks.choose) and fx_slot (plan.py's slot picker) act after the writing; analytics records the arm as assigned and what was used ({factor}_used) and judges the arm as assigned. A channel's own proven difference (10 of its Shorts, its own proof) is in analytics/channel_drivers.csv and overrides the pooled winner there. analytics/tests.json and the hub show each factor's result so far.

evolve_note: 26 October, the self-evolving round (pipeline/evolve.py, evolve.yml at 07:23 UTC): it keeps the test round full by itself. width is 13, two above round 1's 11 factors, so writing-instruction contests run beside round 1 from the first day (the arms are independent 50/50 draws, so an extra factor costs the others no Shorts). Each day it reads analytics/round.csv, retires settled contests (a winner becomes a champion in analytics/evolve.json, an even or unclear factor waits retest_days before a retest), and opens new contests up to width, at most max_changes_per_run a day, from four sources picked by Thompson sampling on each source's record: neighbour (an arm never tried against the champion), retest (a settled factor tried again, a champion against its best rival), gene (a writing instruction, 20 to 220 characters, checked against the channel rules, tested as instruction against none) and mutate (a refined child of an adopted gene, tested against its parent). The proposals are the complex step, so Claude makes them (Charlie, 26 October: complex work uses Claude, day to day work uses free models): model is the Claude model, claude_calls_per_run caps the calls a run (one call returns three proposals and the first valid one is taken), and the free models answer only when Claude returns nothing. Everything else is plain code. Each gene records which model proposed it. A gene that wins is adopted into the recipe on every Short (at most max_adopted, the oldest is retested against no instruction when over); one that loses is rejected. Each contest is a two arm factor drawn 50/50 on every Short (writer.test_plan) and judged from its own start date (drivers.round_verdicts starts). The record is analytics/evolve.json, the log analytics/evolve_log.csv and the summary analytics/evolve.md. Set on to false to go back to the fixed test_round above, or delete analytics/evolve.json to start again from it.
analysis_note: 28 October, false-winner control and re-testing (Charlie approved, serving the Partner Programme). fdr_q: every verdict pass (drivers.csv, channel_drivers.csv, round.csv, the joint model's interactions) computes the p-value of the same t test its interval uses and applies Benjamini-Hochberg across the pass (pipeline/fdr.py); a push, cut back or winner also needs its q at or under fdr_q, else it shows as an early sign or as running with the luck check noted. confirm_share and confirm_n: an adopted winner (an evolve champion or adopted gene) stays in the round as a confirming contest, taken by 1 - confirm_share of the Shorts, the previous choice keeping confirm_share of them, until confirm_n Shorts a side are measured; it is then locked in unless it is worse than the previous choice beyond the even band (0.14 log, 10 percent for engaged-share factors), else reverted with a row in analytics/decisions.csv (evolve.settle_confirm). confirm_n 0 locks a winner in at once, as before.

writer_test.note: 24 October, data report item 7: groq gpt-oss-120b (2.61x day-adjusted, n 7) against Gemini Flash for the writing step, 6 boards in 10 drawn 50/50 by board number (factpack.writer_test) while both have a model this run; the other 4 in 10 go by the writer's own pick, and the 35% cap on the model that actually writes still holds, so each arm sits near 30% of the day. Boards record writer_arm (assigned) and writer_arm_used; drivers.py judges the arm as assigned.

freellm_note: 27 October (Charlie: more free capacity for the writers, fact packs and the learning loop, never stalled when the strong free models run out): pipeline/freellm.py, run by the composite action .github/actions/freellm in trends.yml, write.yml and evolve.yml, starts FreeLLMAPI (github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi, MIT) in Docker on the runner for the job. It fails open: no FREELLM_KEY, no change. The image is pinned (tag v0.16.6, over 7 days old; the first run records its digest here when it is empty, a later pull with another digest refuses to start). The router gets only the keyless free tiers (Kilo and OVHcloud chat; Parallel and Keenable search, which v0.16.6 does not have yet, so with this release web search needs one of the optional keys below) and keys for platforms Quickplay does not call directly (Tavily, Exa, Firecrawl, Linkup, Ollama Cloud, LLM7; optional secrets); never the Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral, Cloudflare, SambaNova or Claude keys. factpack.py offers its top top_models text models (and freellm:auto as the catch-all before Gemini Lite) like any keyed provider, and its web search finds extra sources for a topic with under 3 pages, at most search_per_run searches a run; every fact still passes verify(). status/freellm.json and the hub's Accounts tab show it. GitHub Models is not offered: the router's source says GitHub retired it on 30 July 2026.
shorts_per_day_note: Shorts a day we choose to make, under the learned ceiling (daily_limit): 15 from 24 October, a test of fewer, better Shorts against the 24 to 40 a day before (Charlie, 23 October). 24 October: the test runs 14 days and analytics.volume_test judges it from Sunday 8 November on each UK day's numbers (daily YouTube views and the day's Shorts' 24-hour views, each with a 90% interval over days), not on the 7-day ratio first planned, whose noise (about 19%) can't tell 0.9x from 1.1x. 15 stays unless both are clearly lower (interval top under 0.9); then back to the days before's median number. status/volume.json carries the reading meanwhile. Slots: this many a day at the learned best times.

note: Three writer runs a day (see runs): 20:50 writes the first part of tomorrow, 06:50 and 12:50 write from the day's trends. daily_limit is Shorts made per day, slots_per_day how many go public a day (all 24 hours from 07:30, every 36 minutes, until learned slots take over), upload_limit_24h how many uploads GitHub attempts in 24 hours. background_note: The video behind every Short (pipeline/background.py), 19 October. A board lists 2 to 4 stock searches in "background"; plan.py picks one clip per search (Pexels first, then Pixabay, NASA for a nasa: search; never a clip used in the last reuse_days days), render3 blurs (blur) and darkens (target_luma is the average brightness 0 to 1; a clip darker than min_luma is refused, a dim one is lifted at most max_gain times; brightness above knee, 0 to 255, is squeezed so bright spots never wash out the captions), cross-fades (fade seconds) and plays them under everything, about 8 to 15 seconds each (clip_seconds). Photos then sit on top as cards; real video of the subject still plays full screen. enabled true (since the 19 October test renders): every Short gets it unless its board says "bgvideo": false; with false, only boards with "bgvideo": true do (test boards). Needs the PEXELS_API_KEY and PIXABAY_API_KEY secrets; with neither, or no clip found, a Short renders the old full-screen way.
tiktok_note: off (Charlie, 19 Oct 2026): TikTok blocked every post as spam. Stays off until Charlie has checked the app's Account status page (docs/TIKTOK.md). TikTok does not audit tools that post to their owner's own account, so there is no automatic public posting: inbox (drafts Charlie finishes in the app, at most tiktok_per_day in 24 hours, never over TikTok's 5 pending) or manual. direct posts only with the privacy creator_info offers and tiktok_privacy names, SELF_ONLY when unset (never public by itself). A spam_risk answer from TikTok writes status/tiktok_safety.json and stops TikTok until that file is deleted. social.py tiktok-stats reads our posts' numbers into analytics/tiktok.csv (read-only).
instagram_note: all: every Short goes to Instagram once public on YouTube, the day's picks first, at most a ramped number in 24 hours: instagram_per_day to start, +instagram_ramp_per_day for each day since the first Reel, up to instagram_target (Meta allows 100 API posts a day; it blocked our API access once, so the ramp is gentle). Shorts public for more than crosspost_max_age_hours are skipped. picks: only the day's picks.
breakout_note: A Short at breakout_times or more the views recent Shorts had at the same age (and at least breakout_min_views) is a breakout: the next run writes a follow-up, from a fresh pack on the subject or from the Short's own pages.
factpack_note: trends.yml builds trends/facts.json after trends.py: Gemini (GEMINI_API_KEY) lists each top topic's facts with the exact sentences, and a fact counts as verified only when those sentences are found word for word in two of the day's reputable pages and its numbers match.
reserve_note: Evergreen Shorts in boards/reserve fill any of the day's slots the writer runs left empty: after reserve_after (UK), up to reserve_per_day a day. In flagged approval mode a reserve Short with nothing flagged needs no approval; a flagged one waits for a 'reserve approve' line.
evergreen_search_note: 25 October (Charlie approved search-led evergreen): evergreen_search_per_day Shorts a day whose subjects come from what people search (pipeline/series.py candidates, writer.search_led_packs): our own search terms (analytics/search_terms.csv), YouTube's search suggestions for the prefixes (why does, what is, how did) and the suffix explained after a rotating handful of each category's seeds, Google Trends related queries when trends/latest.json carries them, and Wikipedia's On this day. The evening and morning runs write one each, the afternoon run whatever is missing. Each is kind evergreen from one Wikipedia article (facts checked word for word), source Search-led in drivers.csv, and a numbered Short of its category's series.

series_note: 25 October (Charlie approved named, numbered series in playlists): one series per category (pipeline/series.py). The writer gives each evergreen Short that is not in the reserve the next number of its category's series, counted over boards/* (series_name, series_no on the board), and the title (pattern in title, 70 characters at most), the alternative title, the description (run_board.description) and the creator comment (engage.py) carry the name and number. The series replaces the franchise test arm on these Shorts (test franchise: series). playlist is an optional playlist id to use instead of creating one; the ids engage.py creates are kept in status/playlists.json (playlists.py: 50 units to create, 50 to add a Short, both through quota.allow). Keep a name to 17 characters so the title fits. seeds are the subjects the search suggestions start from.
playbook_note: 25 October (Charlie approved seasonal playbooks as mini-series): when a watchlist item first reaches launch or surging, watch.py writes a playbook once into status/playbooks.json: the item's first 5 angles (padded with generic ones), one a day, numbered '<Event> #1 to #5' in the titles and gathered in a playlist of the event. Progress is read from the boards (series_key), so a missed angle gets grace_days more days and then the series moves on. The angles are watch topics, so the watch places and watch_share_max still apply.
sub_push_note: 25 October (Charlie: a subscriber push baked into everything, measured not assumed; pipeline/subscribe.py). Two arms, each 50/50 and independent of every other arm: test.sub_push (spoken or none: the Short ends with one short, concrete reason to subscribe tied to its series or category; writer.py, every Short but an exploration Short; the old ending arm follow line is folded into it) and the look's closing (chip or none: a small line in the last 1.5 seconds; templates/looks.json, render3.py). Scored on subscribers gained per 1,000 views against Shorts posted the same UK day (drivers.analyse_subscribers, analytics/subs.csv, feature subs:<name>) with views as the guardrail (drivers.csv scores the same arms). Always on: the creator comment's first line, the description's subscribe link, the Instagram caption's last line, the end of a reply. handle: the main channel's, for the subscribe link (https://www.youtube.com/<handle>?sub_confirmation=1; the channel id's link when empty). spoken_share: the share of Shorts that get the spoken line until the data proves an arm. cadence: {series name: how often it comes, e.g. every day}, only where Charlie knows the rhythm is kept (a category is every day: each has a daily floor; a series with no entry gets no promise of a day or time). times: {series or category: hour to name in the spoken line, e.g. two}, only where the posting time is really fixed; empty because slots move round the clock.
upload_limit_note: The ceiling learns (quota.py, status/upload_limit.json): from daily_limit it rises by upload_limit_step after each filled day YouTube accepted everything (no refusal in 48 hours), up to upload_limit_max (72 x 100 units leaves the API allowance room for the extras), and settles where YouTube first refuses (uploadLimitExceeded). The writer's runs, the slots and the hourly uploads all follow it; each change is a line in analytics/decisions.csv.
models_note: Writer models (pipeline/factpack.py writing_order): a Short is written best writer first: the strongest keyed free models (GROQ_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY, SAMBANOVA_API_KEY, CF_API_TOKEN, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, CEREBRAS_API_KEY secrets; big chat models such as GPT-OSS 120B or DeepSeek V3.1; 'providers' here can pin model lists), Gemini Flash (240 s), Gemma, weaker keyed models, then only when all else failed Gemini Lite, the open model on the runner (local_model) and Claude. Claude (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, Charlie's own allowance; claude_model, claude_max_per_run calls a run) also edits a share of passing boards (title, comment, first and last lines; claude_edit_share of them, at most claude_edits_per_day) and can write test-arm boards (claude_writes_per_day; 0 since 24 October), counted per UK day in status/claude_usage.json. analytics/models.json scores writers, editors and pairs; the writer picks from that and Claude's shares fall back when its Shorts earn no more views.
runs_note: Shorts each writer run makes. evening (20:50) writes the first part of TOMORROW (created = tomorrow, slots from 07:30) so flagged ones can be approved before bed; morning (06:50) and afternoon (12:50) write from that day's fresh trends.

facebook_probe_note: Facebook probe (24 October: 54 Reels had 1 play between them and Meta set a spam limit on 23 October): 1 Reel a day (facebook_per_day) with a short caption (the title and facebook_hashtags hashtags, no link) until the probe has run a week and the Reels posted 1 to 8 days ago number facebook_probe_min_reels or more with median plays of facebook_probe_min_plays or more; then it clears by itself (status/facebook_probe.json, a line in analytics/decisions.csv) and the ramp resumes from that day. Set facebook_probe false to end it by hand.
instagram_pick_note: category (the default from 24 October): Instagram picks its own Reels by how each category does on Instagram (social.ig_category_scores: median Instagram views per category over the median, shrunk by 5 Reels; under 15 measured Reels, instagram_category_order first), 1 in 4 an exploration pick from any category (instagram_explore_share), newest first, at most instagram_max_per_run a run. order: the day's picks first, then by publish time. views_3h: a Short waits until it has been public 3 hours and Instagram's room goes to the most watched on YouTube first. views_3h is not used because on 24 October our 96 Shorts with both numbers showed YouTube views at 3 hours do not predict Instagram views (rank correlation 0.10; the top half by 3-hour views had a median of 71 Instagram views, the bottom half 90).
clips_paused_note: Charlie, 26 October: the clips earned no views, so the three clip channels post original Shorts (shorts_channels gaming, irl, clips) and clipping is paused from this date: clips.yml's scheduled runs stop at its Batch time? step (a push to requests/clips* or a workflow_dispatch still runs), clips.py returns at once on a scheduled run, alerts.py drops the clips stale alert, mac_rows.py lists no Vyro rows or campaigns to join (the Mac's Chrome task stays on for the Monday related-video job, one-offs, issues and the poll; it stops at NOTHING TO DO otherwise). Everything uploaded stays up. To clip again once the channels have traction: set this to "".
instagram_first_note: Instagram as its own product (25 October, social.py): a Short in a category Instagram favours goes out at the first run after it is public, whatever its YouTube views (the picker never reads them), inside the posting hour test's rules (a morning-arm Short waits for instagram_morning_hours). Favoured = a category whose Instagram score (ig_category_scores: median Instagram views of its Reels over everyone's, shrunk by 5 Reels) is instagram_favour_min or more; a category in instagram_category_order stays favoured until Instagram has numbers for it (under 15 measured Reels, only that order counts). Favoured and exploration Reels share the top tier, newest first, so a fresh favoured Short is not held behind an older one; the rest follow by score. instagram_first false puts the order back to score first. instagram_hashtags: 3 to 5 family-friendly UK English tags per category, used by the short-caption arm (the long arm keeps the board's own hashtags; a category with no set falls back to the board's first 3). The cover frame (thumb_offset at the hook) is recorded on each post as accepted, refused or off; a refusal stops it being asked for instagram_cover_pause_days days (status/instagram_cover.json) and the tally is in status/social.json (instagram.cover) and status/instagram.json. status/instagram.json and the Instagram section of analytics/insights.md are rewritten by every full analytics run (social.ig_report); the hub's Insights tab reads the file.
instagram_tests_note: Instagram's own tests (24 October, social.py): trial reels for instagram_trial_share of Reels (trial_params with graduation_strategy instagram_trial_strategy: shown first to non-followers, graduated by Meta when they do well; in the Content Publishing API since 3 December 2025 for Instagram Login apps; off for 14 days after Meta refuses one, status/instagram_trial.json); a short caption (the spoken hook and the category's own hashtags, instagram_hashtags) for instagram_caption_share against the full one; instagram_hour_share of Reels held to instagram_morning_hours (UK) against posting as soon as public, each arm with its share of the day's cap; the cover frame (thumb_offset) inside the opening beat. Each arm is fixed per Short by its id and recorded on the post; analytics scores them against Instagram views (drivers.analyse_instagram, never put to the writer) and a proven arm then takes 80% of Reels, never all. Cap: instagram_per_day (4) to start and after Meta pushes back, +instagram_ramp_per_day a day up to instagram_target (8, the data report's cap).

accounts.note: The identity guard (pipeline/identity.py, audit.yml): everything the automation signs in to must be the studio Google account or an account hanging off it, all named Quickplay. The audit checks every sign-in live; a mismatch opens a security issue and stops every posting workflow (identity.py gate).
accounts.secrets_note: Every secret a workflow may read. A new one is added here on purpose, by hand; the audit flags any other.

watch_share_note: 24 October: at most this share of the day's Shorts target goes to watchlist items (launch first, then surging, then build-up), so big dates never crowd out the day's news or any category. Items take after_days (launch week length after the date, 7 unless set) and places (an item's own ceiling a day).
viral_note: 27 October (Charlie: a topic going viral, the Ballon d'Or say, is pushed lots on a rolling basis and its angles tested): pipeline/watch.py viral_items lifts a topic seen on min_sources free trend sources (Wikipedia at min_wiki_views a day, Google Trends, Google News UK, YouTube charts, Bluesky) and rising (momentum times its usual Wikipedia views) into the watchlist for days days: places a day (extra_share of the day's target beyond watch_share_max), one angle a Short (latest, why, reaction, records, explained, facts; watch.VIRAL_DEFAULTS angles), a once angle made once, a daily one once a day. Never unsafe, grim or political topics; never event or broadcast footage. analytics columns viral and viral_angle: drivers.csv rules on the push and each angle (the views gained beyond the topic's own heat). "on": false stops it.
pictures_note: 27 October (Charlie: more relevant content in every Short, the Ballon d'Or winner with the trophy rather than generic stock): fetch_media.rescue gives a shot whose picture scores under floor (pictures.py relevance, 0 to 1) a picture of the beat's named subject: the free lead picture of their English Wikipedia article and their Commons photos, ranked against the beat, taken only when it scores margin (a stock video: video_margin, its motion is worth something) or more above the picture it replaces; a shot that found nothing tries the same before borrowing a nearby beat's picture. At most max_per_short a Short. Never broadcast or event footage (other creators' footage). pic_low_share, pic_rescued and the drivers factor pic_band measure it. on: false restores the first picture found.
daily_sponsor_note: 25 October: while a campaign with "daily": true is live in clips/campaigns.json (a sound or brand hashtag paid per 1,000 views on Quickplay Daily's own Shorts, no footage and no Partner Programme; pipeline/sponsor.py), this share of the Shorts, drawn by board id and recorded as test.sponsor, carries it: the sound as the music, #ad and the campaign hashtags first, YouTube paid promotion on, a clips/submit.csv row for the Vyro or Content Rewards job. Nothing changes while none is live.
community_note: 25 October: from this hour (UTC) the hourly engage run writes status/community.json once a day from the day's best Short at 3 hours (pipeline/community.py): a poll and a one-line post with its link, which the Mac posts on the Community tab.
claude_api_note: 24 October: with an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret (Charlie's monthly Max API credits, claimed in claude.ai Settings, Billing) the pipeline's Claude calls use the Messages API at claude_api_effort instead of the CLI and his chat allowance; the same caps apply (claude_max_per_run, claude_edits_per_day).
apify_note: 25 October (Charlie): the morning trends run (RUN=morning) adds an Apify trend feed when the APIFY_TOKEN secret exists: config apify_feeds lists actors (default apify/google-trends-scraper, related and rising queries for the seed terms), at most apify_max_results items a run ($0.30 per 1,000 on the free plan's $5 monthly credit). Topics carry the source label Apify, so drivers.csv scores the feed like every source.
game_shows_note: 25 October: for a Short about one of these shows, the game's vocabulary (traitor, faithful, betray, murder, banish) passes the excluded-word and negative-framing checks (validate.py); other negative words about real people are still rejected.
sameness_note: 28 October (pipeline/sameness.py, YouTube's inauthentic-content policy refuses channels whose videos feel interchangeable): a draft over max_pair against any Short of its channel in the last window_days days is rewritten once, then dropped; a recipe (format + hook type + look + series) holding recipe_share_max of the window makes the next Short take another format (mega trends and the reserve exempt); alert = a channel's mean pairwise score over this two days running opens an issue. max_pair is the 97th percentile of the highest similarity each of the 178 main-channel boards had to the boards before it (0.295); the 97th percentile of all pairs (0.18) would flag 65% of boards, because a board is compared with 200 or more.
control_note: 28 October (pipeline/control.py): board number k is a control Short with probability share (random.Random(f'control:{k}'), only normal quota Shorts of the main channel); written with analytics/control_recipe.json, the recipe as frozen on that day, no round arm, gene or exploration; left out of every verdict; trend.py compares the loop's Shorts with them (needs min_n control Shorts).
